title: Acid-driven defect engineering in MoS 2 : bridging experimental advances with mechanistic and characterisation insights toward sustainable energy and environmental applications
content: The advancement of the energy and environmental sectors demands innovative and sustainable strategies to address global challenges, including clean energy generation, pollution control, and resource management, thereby directly contributing to SDGs 6 and 7. Among emerging materials, molybdenum disulphide (MoS2) has gained significant attention in recent years due to its tunable band gap, large surface area, and remarkable catalytic properties, making it highly suitable for energy conversion and environmental remediation applications. However, its practical performance is mostly restricted by poor conductivity, limited active-site accessibility, and sluggish charge-transfer kinetics. Defect engineering has been established as an excellent approach for overcoming such challenges, and the use of acidic surface treatments has become of great interest due to their scalability, chemical tunability, proton intercalation, sulphur vacancy formation, interlayer spacing, and surface functionalisation. These transformations significantly enhance the performance of MoS2 in hydrogen evolution reactions, photocatalysis, batteries, supercapacitors, membrane separations, and antibacterial applications. This review provides a cohesive mechanistic framework that links acid chemistry, defect formation, and performance-related properties. It offers an in-depth discussion of the interconnections among structure, properties, and performance. It also discusses density functional theory (DFT) studies aimed at understanding vacancy energetics and phase stability. Finally, problems such as defect instability, oxidation beyond the desired level, scalability and reproducibility are also addressed.
